messages:
nic: Quick one — we're still fuzzy on how hosted/dedicated/private should treat control-plane flags vs manifest pins. I sketched three modes: authoritative, advisory, and offline-only.

maya: Sketch the semantics?

nic: authoritative = control-plane can override manifest (hosted default). advisory = control-plane suggests but manifest wins (private default). offline-only = control-plane never used, only local manifest and heuristics.

tj: Operationally, need signed policy snapshots for advisory/authoritative so private can verify. Also include snapshot_id + ttl + sig.

sanju: Agree. Add a small precedence table in shim: manifest_pin -> snapshot(policy) -> local_heuristic. But if manifest sets "control_authoritative: true" then snapshot takes precedence.

harper: For air-gapped installs, support artifact delivery: redwoodctl snapshot sign -> tarball that ops can import. Bring-your-own-sig allowed.

nic: Telemetry: when a fallback or override happens, emit minimal shim_event: {snapshot_id, manifest_hash, decision, len_tokens, latency_ms}. No prompt content. Buffer locally if no egress.

maya: Circuit breakers: client must support local fast-fail when p95>latency_threshold or X 5xxs. Control plane can suggest thresholds but client must be able to act offline.

tj: Emergency-off: control plane can publish revocation list of snapshot_ids; clients must check on reconnect. Also a local emergency toggle guarded by admin creds.

sanju: Policy format: tiny JSONL or proto with fields: route, action(allow|warn|deny|fallback), fallback_target, max_seq_len, qos_hint. Keep it compact.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling 5% -> control-flag "fast_qs" enabled (ts 4822001150)

harper: API surfaces: expose Shim.fetchSnapshot(), Shim.getEffectivePolicy(route) -> returns policy + provenance string (manifest|snapshot:<id>|local). Keep response small.

nic: UX: make manifest param "policy_influence": "none"|"advisory"|"authoritative" with default "advisory" for private packages. Document upgrade path.

maya: Also include policy_ttl_seconds and cache_ttl so shims know when to revalidate.

tj: Owners: maya -> manifest docs and CLI examples; harper -> shims API and sample code; sanju -> telemetry envelope + privacy; I'll write rollout checklist.

nic: Ok final question: should hosted treat advisory snapshots as authoritative during canary windows? i.e. temporary override.

sanju: Yes, but only if manifest allows it via a short-lived opt-in flag; otherwise treat advisory as advisory.

maya: I'll wire that into manifest docs and add an explicit canary_opt_in field.

nic: Great. I'll file RFC with snapshot proto, manifest additions, shim API and rollout checklist. Marking this resolved for architecture followup. :white_check_mark:
